text_with_mask: High entropy alloys are typically composed of five or more principal elements in [MASK] or near-equal atomic proportions.
The configurational entropy of a high entropy alloy tends to be [MASK] than that of a conventional single-principal-element alloy.
A face-centered cubic high entropy alloy generally exhibits [MASK] ductility than a body-centered cubic one.
Refractory high entropy alloys are typically alloyed with elements such as niobium, tantalum, molybdenum, and [MASK].
Grain refinement generally leads to an [MASK] in yield strength, consistent with the Hall-Petch relationship.
Solid solution strengthening in high entropy alloys arises largely from atomic size [MASK] between the constituent elements.
Body-centered cubic high entropy alloys are generally [MASK] and less ductile than face-centered cubic ones at room temperature.
Increasing the aluminum content in a CoCrFeNi-based alloy tends to promote a transition from FCC to [MASK] structure.
